chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all together, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:
Muhammad ibn Hamza al-Alawi wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) the second: 'A master of yours bequeathed to me one hundred dirhams, and I used to hear him say,

He wrote to him: 'Look to hand over from these dirhams to the two wives of the man, and their right from that is one-eighth, if he had a child. If he did not have a child, then one-quarter, and give in charity with the remainder upon whomever you know has need of it, God willing.'

key_terms.زَوْجَتَيِ الرَّجُلِ: the two wives of the man

ai.seo_question: How is an estate distributed when a man dies with two wives but no children and no will?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the application of the 'Thumn' (one-eighth) rule for wives in the absence of descendants, a specific nuance in Shia inheritance jurisprudence. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) directs that after allocating the wives' shares, the remainder is to be distributed as charity to those in need, highlighting the dual role of inheritance and voluntary benevolence in small estates. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Shia fiqh in handling minor estates where formal heirs are limited.
